title: Cascade framework for company OKRs and stakeholder alignment
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a repeatable cascade and communications framework so company-level OKRs become clear, measurable, and owned by product, engineering, and design partners. This ticket captures the matrix, stakeholder roles, cadence, handoffs, and communication artifacts required to align initiatives across Redwood Inference for 2026 planning.

Context: Past quarters showed good OKR definition at the exec layer but uneven downstream adoption. Teams report confusion about which initiatives map to each company objective, who owns success metrics, and what to surface during weekly syncs. This work reduces cognitive load for squad leads and speeds decision-making for Dedicated/Private product initiatives that require multi-team coordination.

Deliverables:
- Initiative-to-OKR matrix template (CSV + Confluence page) that maps owner, success metrics, key results, and blocked dependencies.
- RACI for company-level initiatives with named backups and escalation path.
- Communication playbook: triage cadence, weekly dashboard digest, and executive decision windows.
- Onboarding checklist for new Initiative Leads (template + 1-pager).
- Pilot with 3 active initiatives (Serving runtime throughput, Console rollouts, Private deployment upgrade flow).

Scope & Boundaries: Focus is company-level cascade and cross-functional alignment; squad-level task planning remains in team backlogs. This is not a performance review or comp calibration change. We will not change existing tooling integrations (Linear, Confluence, Looker) in this phase — instead we provide templates and lightweight automations using webhooks.

Trade-offs considered:
- Granularity vs. speed: We chose a 1-page matrix per initiative (owner + 3 metrics) instead of a full PRD to keep cadence fast.
- Centralization vs. empowerment: We will not require all teams to follow the template strictly; the adoption target is 80% for initiatives that intersect more than one department.

Acceptance criteria (summary): Initiative matrix in Confluence for 3 pilots; RACI approved by Eng/Product/Design leads; weekly digest automated; first readout with execs and follow-up action list created.
acceptance_criteria: Confluence initiative matrix template published and linked in central OKR hub
3 pilot initiatives populated with owners, 3 measurable KR targets, and dependencies
RACI table reviewed and signed-off by Clara Nguyen (Design), Omar Li (Eng), and Seth Romero (Security)
Weekly dashboard digest automatically delivered to #company-okrs Slack channel
Post-pilot survey shows >75% of stakeholders agree alignment improved

2026-01-08 - Cross-functional review session: Decided on 1-page matrix approach to keep leadership review meetings under 45 minutes. Trade-off: less detail for faster iteration. Action: schedule bi-weekly syncs and a monthly executive readout.

2026-01-22 - Omar Li (Eng): Confirmed backup owners for all initiatives and proposed an escalation path into SRE on-call if an initiative breaches latency SLOs. Linked ENG-3112 for the SRE automation task.
